name: DHS Science & Technology SBIR Cybersecurity Topics
provider: U.S. Department of Homeland Security (S&T Directorate)
description: DHS S&T SBIR solicitations frequently fund small businesses developing cybersecurity and critical-infrastructure-protection technologies.
eligibility: US-based small businesses developing R&D-stage cybersecurity technology.
funding_amount_text: Phase I typically ~$150,000-$200,000; Phase II typically ~$1,000,000
how_to_apply: Respond to open topic solicitations via DHS SBIR portal.
notes: Part of the federal SBIR/STTR program, reauthorized through FY2031.

name: DoD SBIR/STTR Cybersecurity Topics
description: Small Business Innovation Research / Small Business Technology Transfer solicitations that regularly include cybersecurity, secure systems, and cyber-resilience topic areas across DoD components.
eligibility: US-based small businesses (for-profit, <500 employees per SBA size standards) developing R&D-stage technology.
funding_amount_text: Phase I typically ~$150,000-$250,000; Phase II typically ~$1,000,000+ (varies by solicitation)
application_status: Periodic solicitation cycles; programs reauthorized through FY2031 as of April 2026
how_to_apply: Respond to open topic solicitations on the DoD SBIR/STTR portal.
notes: SBIR/STTR reauthorized April 13, 2026 through FY2031; new Phase II 'Strategic Breakthrough' award vehicle up to $30M ceiling; up to $6,500 (Phase I) / $50,000 (Phase II) may be used for cybersecurity support and technical assistance.

name: NSF SBIR/STTR Secure & Trustworthy Computing Topics
description: NSF SBIR/STTR solicitations include cybersecurity and secure/trustworthy computing topic areas for early-stage small-business R&D.
eligibility: US-based small businesses developing R&D-stage cybersecurity technology.
funding_amount_text: Phase I up to ~$305,000; Phase II up to ~$1,250,000 (amounts adjusted periodically)
application_status: Rolling submission windows several times per year
how_to_apply: Submit a project pitch via the NSF SBIR/STTR portal.
notes: Part of the federal SBIR/STTR program, reauthorized through FY2031.

name: SBA Cybersecurity for Small Business Pilot Program
description: SBA pilot program awarding grants to state agencies/universities to deliver cybersecurity training, counseling, and tailored services to startups and emerging small businesses. FY2024-FY2026 awards went to Dakota State University, Eastern Washington University, and the University of Texas at San Antonio.
eligibility: Small businesses access services indirectly through the funded state/university partners (training, counseling, assessments); the direct grantees are state agencies and universities.
application_status: Pilot program; performance period ends September 2026 - watch SBA.gov for renewal/expansion
how_to_apply: Small businesses should contact the funded partner institutions directly for free training/counseling; the grant itself is awarded to institutions, not individual businesses.
notes: Not a direct-to-business cash grant; funds free cybersecurity services delivered by pilot institutions.

name: CGA CMMC Tooling Grant
description: In-kind grant covering tools/software needed to pursue Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) compliance, aimed at defense-industrial-base small businesses.
eligibility: Small businesses pursuing CMMC compliance (e.g., DoD contractors/subcontractors).
how_to_apply: Apply via the Cyber Grants Alliance website.
notes: In-kind (service/tool credit), not cash.

name: CGA Employee Cybersecurity Training Grant
description: In-kind grant funding employee cybersecurity awareness training for qualifying small businesses.
eligibility: Small businesses seeking employee security-awareness training.
how_to_apply: Apply via the Cyber Grants Alliance website.
notes: In-kind (training credit), not cash.

name: CGA Penetration Testing Grant
description: In-kind grant covering a professional penetration test for a qualifying small business.
eligibility: Small businesses wanting a funded pen test.
how_to_apply: Apply via the Cyber Grants Alliance website.
notes: In-kind (service credit), not cash.

name: CISA/FEMA State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program (SLCGP)
provider: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) / FEMA
description: $1B (FY2022-FY2026) federal program funding state/local cybersecurity planning and implementation. Only State Administrative Agencies (SAAs) may apply directly; states may sub-award portions to local governments and, in some states, to small businesses supporting critical infrastructure.
eligibility: Direct applicants are State Administrative Agencies. Small businesses may benefit only through state-run sub-award/pass-through programs - check your state's SAA.
application_status: Concludes active funding phase in FY2026; performance period runs through FY2029
how_to_apply: Small businesses cannot apply directly - contact your state's Administrative Agency to ask about local sub-award opportunities.
notes: Pass-through only; not a direct small-business grant, but the largest federal cybersecurity grant pool. Listed for awareness of state sub-programs (e.g., Massachusetts, Wisconsin, California below).

name: California SLCGP (Cal OES)
provider: California Governor's Office of Emergency Services (Cal OES)
description: California's state-administered share of the federal SLCGP, funding cybersecurity planning and implementation for eligible entities statewide.
eligibility: Local governments and eligible partner entities in California; small-business eligibility varies by sub-award cycle.
how_to_apply: Apply through Cal OES SLCGP program office.
notes: Example of a state SLCGP pass-through program; verify current eligibility for private businesses each cycle.

name: Cyber Resilient Massachusetts Grant Program
description: State grant program (NOFO 2026-Cyber-01) funding Security Operations Center (SOC) services for up to three years for eligible municipalities, small businesses, and nonprofits in Massachusetts.
eligibility: Small businesses, municipalities, and nonprofits located in Massachusetts.
application_status: Open per NOFO 2026-Cyber-01 - check MassCyberCenter for current cycle dates
how_to_apply: Submit application per the Notice of Funding Opportunity published by MassCyberCenter.
notes: One of the few state programs that funds small businesses directly for cybersecurity services (SOC-as-a-service).

name: CyberCert Silver Certification Grant
description: In-kind grant covering the cost of obtaining CyberCert Silver cybersecurity certification for a small business.
eligibility: Small businesses seeking baseline cybersecurity certification.
how_to_apply: Apply via the Cyber Grants Alliance website.
notes: In-kind (service credit), not cash.

name: NIST MEP Cybersecurity Assistance
provider: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Manufacturing Extension Partnership
description: Not a cash grant, but federally-funded technical assistance through MEP Centers to help small manufacturers assess and improve cybersecurity posture (e.g., NIST 800-171 / CMMC readiness).
eligibility: Small and mid-sized manufacturers.
funding_amount_text: Free/subsidized technical assistance (varies by state MEP Center)
how_to_apply: Contact your state's MEP Center.
notes: Service/assistance program rather than a cash award; included because it is a major cybersecurity-protection resource for small manufacturers.

name: Wisconsin SLCGP Sub-Award Funding
provider: Wisconsin Office of the Governor / State Administrative Agency
description: Wisconsin's state-administered share of the federal SLCGP, sub-awarded to eligible local entities for cybersecurity planning, endpoint protection, and infrastructure hardening.
eligibility: Local government entities and, in some cycles, small businesses supporting local critical infrastructure in Wisconsin.
how_to_apply: Apply through Wisconsin's SLCGP state administrative agency portal.
notes: Example of a state SLCGP pass-through program; verify current eligibility for private businesses each cycle.

name: Amber Grant for Women
description: Monthly grant awarding $10,000 to a woman-owned business, with one annual winner from among monthly winners receiving an additional $25,000.
eligibility: Women-owned businesses.
how_to_apply: Apply online via the Amber Grant website ($15 application fee as of last review).
notes: Short, accessible application; good entry point for first-time grant seekers.

name: Comcast RISE
description: Provides free marketing services, technology makeovers (including tech/security-relevant upgrades), and grant funding to small businesses, awarded quarterly.
eligibility: Business operational 1+ years, located within Comcast/Effectv service area, 51%+ owned by a woman or person of color.
funding_amount_text: Marketing/tech services package; monetary grant amount varies by cycle
how_to_apply: Apply online during the open quarterly window.
notes: Includes technology makeovers that can cover cybersecurity/IT upgrades for winning businesses.

name: FedEx Small Business Grant Contest
description: Annual contest awarding grants to innovative small businesses, judged on business merit and community impact.
eligibility: US-based small businesses (specific size/revenue criteria set each cycle).
how_to_apply: Apply during the annual open window via the FedEx Small Business Grant Contest site.
notes: Highly competitive annual contest; watch for the application window each year.

name: Grants.gov (Federal Grant Portal)
description: The central federal clearinghouse for all federally funded grant opportunities, including cybersecurity and small-business programs. Not a grant itself - a search/alert tool.
eligibility: Varies by individual opportunity listed.
how_to_apply: Create a free account, set keyword alerts (e.g., 'cybersecurity', 'small business'), and filter by eligibility.
notes: Use this as an ongoing discovery tool alongside this database.

name: Hello Alice Small Business Grants
provider: Hello Alice (with corporate partners: eBay, FedEx, H&R Block, Allstate, DoorDash, PayPal, and others)
description: Ongoing series of corporate-sponsored grant programs distributed through the Hello Alice platform; has distributed $57M+ in grant capital to small business owners.
eligibility: Varies per specific grant program; create a Hello Alice business profile to match to open opportunities.
application_status: Rolling - new programs open throughout the year
how_to_apply: Create a free business profile at helloalice.com and apply to matched open grants.
notes: Aggregator of many corporate-sponsored grants; check regularly as new cycles open.

name: SBA FAST (Federal and State Technology Partnership)
description: Helps states build infrastructure and outreach to increase small-business participation in SBIR/STTR programs, including cybersecurity R&D topics.
eligibility: State/regional economic development or technology organizations (not individual businesses directly).
how_to_apply: State technology development organizations apply directly; small businesses benefit from resulting SBIR/STTR outreach and support services.
notes: Indirect benefit to small businesses via improved state SBIR/STTR support infrastructure.

name: SBA Growth Accelerator Fund Competition
description: Cash-prize competition for accelerators, incubators, and other ecosystem organizations that support underrepresented entrepreneurs, including tech and cyber-adjacent founders.
eligibility: Accelerators/incubators/ecosystem organizations (not individual businesses directly).
how_to_apply: Apply via SBA's Growth Accelerator Fund Competition portal when open.
notes: Awarded to ecosystem organizations, which often support cybersecurity startups among their portfolio.

name: SBA PRIME (Program for Investment in Microentrepreneurs)
description: Funds nonprofit organizations that provide training and technical assistance to low-income and disadvantaged microentrepreneurs.
eligibility: Direct grantees are nonprofit microenterprise development organizations; microentrepreneurs benefit indirectly through training/services.
how_to_apply: Nonprofits apply via Grants.gov; microentrepreneurs contact local PRIME grantees for services.
notes: Pass-through program; not direct cash to individual businesses.

name: SBA SCALE (Supply Chain Acceleration and Logistics Enablement) Program
description: SBA program announced with $9 million in grant funding (July 2026) supporting small businesses in supply-chain and logistics resilience.
eligibility: Eligible small businesses in supply chain/logistics sectors - check current NOFO for specifics.
application_status: Announced July 2026 - check SBA.gov for application window
how_to_apply: Follow the official Notice of Funding Opportunity on SBA.gov.
notes: Recently announced (July 2026); confirm current application status before relying on this entry.

name: SBA STEP (State Trade Expansion Program)
description: Funds state governments to help small businesses start or expand exporting, including trade-show grants, export training, and market entry support.
eligibility: Small businesses pursuing export growth, accessed through their state's STEP-awarded agency.
how_to_apply: Apply through your state's designated STEP administering agency.
notes: Funds flow through states; check your state's economic development office for current cycle.

name: SBA Women's Business Centers (WBC) Program
description: Funds a national network of Women's Business Centers providing free/low-cost training, counseling, and access-to-capital assistance, including for tech and cybersecurity-sector founders.
eligibility: WBCs are the direct grantees; entrepreneurs (with emphasis on women) access free services.
funding_amount_text: Free/low-cost services to entrepreneurs; center grants vary
application_status: Ongoing services; center funding is annual
how_to_apply: Find and contact your nearest Women's Business Center.
notes: Service/counseling program, not direct cash grants to businesses.
